MGIMS Organises Gandhi Jayanti Eye Camp
Friday, 03 October 2025
1267 Hits
On 2nd October 2025, the Department of Ophthalmology at MGIMS organised a one-day free Gandhi Jayanti Eye Camp, commemorating the 156th birth anniversary of the Father of the Nation. Launched more than 25 years ago, this initiative has grown into a beacon of hope for patients in Wardha and neighbouring districts.
This year’s camp, held at the Eye OPD of Kasturba Hospital, saw 458 patients (294 male and 164 female) undergo comprehensive eye examinations for conditions ranging from cataracts and glaucoma to refractive errors and other vision-related ailments. Patients travelled from towns and villages across Vidarbha and adjoining states to avail themselves of these free services.
Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Smita Singh, Director Professor & Head of Ophthalmology, reiterated the vision behind the camp: “Restoring eyesight goes far beyond medical treatment—it restores independence, dignity, and hope. In the coming week, we will be conducting free cataract surgeries for 111 patients identified in this camp, ensuring that no one is burdened by cost.” She also acknowledged the tireless efforts of the ophthalmology team and support staff in making the camp successful.
Sharing his thoughts, Dr. A.K. Shukla, Dean, MGIMS and Director Professor of Ophthalmology, said: “In keeping with the Gandhian ideals of service and compassion instilled in us by Dr. Sushila Nayar, we reaffirm our institutional commitment to community healthcare. Year after year, this initiative reaches patients who otherwise would have limited access to specialized treatment. Through this Gandhi Jayanti Eye Camp, we pay our tribute to Gandhiji’s vision of service to humanity.”
Many patients expressed heartfelt gratitude. One elderly participant from Yavatmal remarked: “I had given up hope of ever seeing clearly again. This camp has given me a second chance at life.”
